text:
Sam Steel hasn't had a point in eleven straight games, and this is one slump our numbers don't wave away. Over his last ten, the Stars have created 5.2 expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice against 6.5 in a normal stretch, and his own looks have thinned out too. He has 1 goal and 3 points in 19 games despite 16:02 a night, a lot of ice for that return.

There is some bad luck mixed in. Across the whole season the Stars have scored 5.7 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on, and he's shooting 5% where our range runs 11% to 16%. That part tends to come back. The drop in chances is the part to worry about.

Steel's value has always been elsewhere: he kills penalties, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 55% of his shots coming off the rush last season, so he lives on quick counters. Evolving-Hockey had him worth 1.1 wins last season. Our projection of 21 to 38 points needs the chances to return first.
